findings.description: The instance user-data embeds an AWS access key ID and secret access key. These credentials are exposed in Terraform state, source control, EC2 user-data metadata, and potentially instance logs, enabling unauthorized AWS API access if retrieved.

SSH (TCP/22) is allowed from 0.0.0.0/0. Because the instance is launched in a public subnet with public IP assignment, this exposes remote administration to internet-wide scanning and brute-force or exploit attempts.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true or specify a KMS key. Unless account-level default EBS encryption is independently enforced, data on this disk is stored unencrypted at rest.

This snapshot is created from an EBS volume that is not configured for encryption. The resulting backup can contain the disk's data without encryption at rest unless encryption is enforced externally.

The bucket receiving VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration. Sensitive network telemetry may be stored without explicit encryption at rest unless a separate account-level policy enforces it.
